thymosin-beta-4.definition: A natural protein of 43 amino acids found in almost every cell. It holds single actin molecules ready for use and has been tested as eye drops and skin gel. It is not the same substance as TB-500.

actin.definition: A protein that forms thin threads inside cells. Cells build and take apart these threads to change shape and to move.

heptapeptide.definition: A peptide made of exactly seven amino acids. TB-500 is a heptapeptide.

n-terminal-acetylation.definition: Adding a small chemical group (an acetyl group) to a molecule. On a peptide it changes the charge and shape of the start of the chain, so it can change how the peptide works and how long it lasts.

free-base-and-salt.definition: The plain form of a drug molecule. A salt form, such as an acetate, is the same molecule paired with a small partner molecule. Regulators treat the two as different substances.

ac-sdkp.definition: A peptide of four amino acids that the body cuts from the start of thymosin beta-4. In animal studies it reduces inflammation and scarring. TB-500 does not contain it.

prolyl-oligopeptidase.definition: An enzyme in the body that cuts proteins just after the amino acid proline. It releases Ac-SDKP from thymosin beta-4.

integrin-linked-kinase.definition: A protein inside cells that passes on signals from the points where the cell holds on to its surroundings. It helps cells survive and move, and it is very active in many cancers.

atp-synthase.definition: An enzyme that makes ATP, the molecule cells use to store energy. A small amount also sits on the outside of some cells, where it can act as a signal.

metastasis.definition: When cancer cells leave the first tumour and grow in another part of the body.

mast-cell.definition: An immune cell found in the skin and other tissues. When it is triggered it releases histamine and other substances that cause itching, redness and swelling.

knockout-mouse.definition: A mouse bred so that one gene is completely switched off. Researchers use it to see what the body needs that gene for.

compassionate-use.definition: Giving an unapproved treatment to a seriously ill patient outside a trial, because other treatments have not worked. It is not a test of whether the treatment works.

neurotrophic-keratopathy.definition: An eye disease in which damaged nerves stop the clear front of the eye (the cornea) from healing. Small wounds on the eye surface stay open and can scar.

dry-eye-disease.definition: A condition in which the eyes make too few tears, or the tears dry too quickly. It causes discomfort and can damage the surface of the eye.

venous-leg-ulcer.definition: An open wound on the lower leg that does not heal for weeks or months. It is caused by poor blood flow back to the heart through the leg veins.

pressure-ulcer.definition: Damage to the skin and the tissue under it, caused by pressure over a long time, for example from lying in bed without moving.

epidermolysis-bullosa.definition: A rare inherited disease in which the skin is so fragile that it blisters and tears after light rubbing.

infarct-size.definition: How much heart muscle has died after a heart attack. Doctors measure it with heart scans.

anti-drug-antibodies.definition: Antibodies that the immune system makes against a medicine. They can make the medicine work less well or cause reactions.

wada-s2-3.definition: The part of the WADA Prohibited List for growth factors and substances that change them, including thymosin beta-4 and TB-500. They are banned in sport at all times.
